title: Prompt Atrophy — lab diary (personal)
content:
Notes to self: exploring 'prompt atrophy' — phenomenon where repeated use of a prompt/template in production seems to degrade instruction-following over time or across long sessions.

Background/context:
- Observed in internal canary for helpdesk summarizer: after ~3000 requests with the same few-shot seed set, the fraction of hallucinated contact details increased.
- Hypothesis: cold-start vs warmed cache interplay + exemplar drift (model shifts when internal KV cache fills, plus token budgets cause template truncation).
- Want to reproduce locally and concoct synthetic experiments that isolate causes: exemplar aging, context truncation, temperature and sampling, model variant (quantized vs fp16 kernel selection).

Experiment log (high-level):
1) Session-sim replay (seq length constant)
   - Setup: 1k synthetic tickets, single template with 5 exemplars, model: rwd-7B-ptq, temp=0.2, top_p=0.95, stream off.
   - Observation: instruction-adherence score (binary) drops from 0.97 @ first 100 to 0.88 @ last 100.
   - Quick check: rerun with caching disabled -> degradation disappears (0.96 -> 0.95). Implication: my earlier hypothesis about cache interactions likely real.

2) Few-shot exemplar aging
   - Rotate exemplars every 100 requests vs fixed exemplar set. Rotating schedule reduces degradation but increases variance.
   - Possible mitigation: exemplar rotation + weighted anchoring (explicit anchor instruction inserted every N requests).

3) Prompt truncation edgecases
   - For long conversations, prefix truncation caused template instructions to be pushed out; move critical instruction into the final step and still see worse outcomes -> indicates effect beyond simple truncation (model internal state influenced by earlier tokens).

4) Thermal/sampling sensitivity
   - Higher temperature magnifies drift; lower temperature stabilizes but reduces creativity. For summarization we prefer stability -> temp 0.0–0.2 recommended for production.

Representative prompt templates tried (keep short):
- Baseline few-shot summarizer:
  "You are a helpful assistant. Example:
   Q: <ticket text>
   A: <summary>
   ... (5 exemplars)
   Now summarize:
   <ticket text>

  Output:"

- Anchored variant:
  "You are a precise summarizer. Use this checklist (always include): 1) one-line summary, 2) category tag, 3) 2-sentence action items. Examples: (3 exemplars)
  ALWAYS END WITH: '---END_SUMMARY---'
  <ticket text>

  Output:"

Failure cases observed (examples paraphrased):
- Repetition loop: model repeats first exemplar phrasing verbatim for multiple inputs mid-session. Suspect KV cache reuse.
- Missing action items: when exemplar count >7, model sometimes omits the third checklist item.
- Hallucinated contact info: rare but correlated with long sessions on same seed.

Metrics to track in future runs (suggested):
- Instruction Adherence (binary per response)
- Extractive Overlap (ROUGE-L vs gold summary)
- Hallucination score (entity halluc count)
- Drift slope (linear fit of adherence over request index)
- KV cache hit/miss trace (if instrumented)

Quick hypotheses and mitigation ideas:
- Cache warm/cold boundary: add randomized prefix tokens to reduce exact cache reuse. Test impact on latency and cost.
- Anchor reinforcement: inject a short anchor instruction every N requests or store anchor in short token-level cache that is never evicted. (Requires runtime change).
- Exemplar rotation + small exemplar pool (3) prioritized by recency and coverage.
- Use deterministic sampling (temp 0, beam 1) for stable tasks; schedule occasional stochastic samples for QA.

Short checklist for reproducible run:
- [ ] Create deterministic synthetic dataset (1k items) with edge cases
- [ ] Instrument KV cache stats in the serving runtime (pull from /metrics or agent trace)
- [ ] Run sessions with and without cache, record adherence and hallucination counts
- [ ] Try rotation strategies (rotate every 50/100/200 reqs)
- [ ] Test with rwd-7B-ptq, rwd-13B-fp16, hosted-13B-quant variants

Open questions / notes:
- Is the KV cache behavior deterministic across model variants or affected by quantization kernel selection? Need SRE/infra help to map cache lifecycle to kernel choices. (Ping Marcus).
- Could model calibration drift be due to tokenization boundary behavior when exemplars contain special characters? Run tokenization-only tests.
- How do rollouts interact—if we shift model variant mid-session, what's the expected degradation vs improvement? Add an A/B stub.

Action items (next week):
- Marcus: add KV cache counters to canary trace (ML-482).
- Me: implement session-replay harness and exemplar rotation code (PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/523)
- Riley: run side-by-side latency/cost tradeoff for anchor insertion (measure extra tokens vs adherence gain).

Misc scratch thoughts:
- Could try embedding-based exemplar retrieval but enforce 'anchor exemplar' that is always appended to the front. Might prevent drift while keeping dynamic retrieval.
- Consider prompt fingerprinting: hash of active template+exemplars logged per response to detect template entropy increases in production.
- Track per-customer drift curves (some tenants might amplify atrophy).

Notes to self: keep this intentionally messy. Aim to produce a short internal note for sketching the mitigation and send to #eng-applied-ml by Friday once we have initial plots.

Recent references/logs: slack thread: #prod-canaries (thread ts: 1698723452.000200), ML-482 ticket for cache counters, small PR above is a prototype.

End of entry for 2025-12-02.

-- Asha
